notes: Each eval targets a failure this theme produces *with a green build*. An eval that only checks 'the build succeeded' proves nothing here. Schema follows the skill-creator evals.json shape.

evals.prompt: Add a grid of three cards to docs/index.md linking to the getting-started, configuration, and reference pages.
evals.expected_output: A `cards` block wrapping three `card` calls, each using only parameters from the whitelist.
expectations: Uses `{{< cards >}}` … `{{< /cards >}}` as a pair, not self-closed
Each `card` uses only title, link, icon, badge, image, or image_alt
Does not invent parameters such as `description`, `text`, or `href`
Any `icon` value is a name from data/icons.json, not a CSS class or Font Awesome name

evals.prompt: This page has a numbered figure. Add a cross-reference to it from an earlier paragraph.
evals.expected_output: A self-closed `xref` with exactly one target kind.
expectations: Writes `{{< xref fig="…" />}}` self-closed, or paired only when supplying custom link text
Passes exactly one of fig, tbl, eq, eg — not several at once
Does not hand-write a label like "Figure 2", since xref generates it per locale

evals.prompt: Write a three-step install procedure for this docs page.
evals.expected_output: An ordered list carrying `{.steps}`, not the steps shortcode.
expectations: Uses an ordered list with `{.steps}` rather than `{{< steps >}}`
If it does use the shortcode, it states the specific reason (TOC entries or a container shortcode inside a step)
Does not self-close the container if the shortcode is used

evals.prompt: Add a Mermaid flowchart showing the request lifecycle to this page.
evals.expected_output: A fenced code block with language `mermaid`.
expectations: Uses a ```mermaid fence
Does not write `{{< mermaid >}}`, which is not a shortcode in this theme

evals.prompt: I'm starting a new site with this theme. Set it up so I can preview it.
evals.expected_output: hugo new site, a complete theme copy including data/, and the required markup config.
expectations: Copies layouts, assets, static, data, and i18n, plus hugo.toml and theme.toml
Explicitly includes data/ — omitting it silently drops every icon
Adds the five markup settings from config.md, not a subset
Does not run `hugo mod get` or add the theme to module.imports
Does not claim `pnpm dev` or `pnpm build` will build the user's own site
Does not require `pnpm install` in order to use the theme

evals.prompt: Code blocks stay light-coloured after switching to dark mode. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies missing `noClasses = false` in the site's markup.highlight.
expectations: Names `[markup.highlight] noClasses = false` as the cause
Explains that Hugo ignores markup settings coming from a theme, so it must be in the site config
Does not propose editing the theme's CSS or the theme's own hugo.toml
Mentions that `noClasses = true` is Hugo's default, so this must be set explicitly

evals.prompt: Search returns nothing on my local dev server. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the Pagefind index does not exist under hugo server.
expectations: States that the index is built from public/ after Hugo runs, so it is absent under `hugo server`
Gives `npx pagefind --site public` as the step
Does not treat this as a theme bug or suggest changing search configuration

evals.prompt: Add a contributors section to the about page.
evals.expected_output: The shortcode plus the data file it depends on.
expectations: Notes that a data/<key>.yaml file is required
Warns that without it the shortcode renders nothing while the build still succeeds
Does not claim the theme fetches contributors from an API

evals.prompt: I set the badge title with `titel=` by mistake and the build passed. Why didn't it fail?
evals.expected_output: Explains warn-plus-fallback, and how to make it fail.
expectations: Explains that unknown parameters warn and are ignored, leaving the build green
Recommends `hugo --printPathWarnings --panicOnWarning`
Notes that `badge` has no `title` parameter at all — the correct one is `text`

evals.prompt: Document these API fields on the reference page: name, timeout, retries.
expectations: Uses `fields` as the container and `field` for each entry
Uses only name, type, required, default on `field`
Does not self-close `fields`, which warns and renders nothing
Puts each field's prose in the body, since that is what gets rendered as Markdown

evals.prompt: Refactor this Go service's error handling.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not trigger — no Hugo or theme content involved.
expectations: Does not load or cite this skill's reference files

evals.prompt: Add a tabbed code sample showing the same request in curl, Python, and Go.
expectations: Uses `tabs` + `tab`, paired
Uses only label and value on `tab`, and group/default/label on `tabs`
Supplies `value` on each tab when `tabs` declares a `group`, since otherwise that tab will not sync
